hook.situation: Explaining a choice that has both good and bad sides, or continuing with a plan despite a problem.
objectives: Use A/V-지만 for clean contrast: 비싸지만 맛있어요.
Use A/V-(으)ㄴ/는데도 when the result is surprising despite the situation: 비가 오는데도 사람이 많아요.
Use V아/어도 when the result stays the same even if the condition happens: 비가 와도 갈 거예요.
hook.whyItMatters: Learners often connect everything with 그리고 or translate every 'but' the same way. Korean separates simple contrast, surprising concession, and 'even if' conditions. This lets plans sound more precise and less flat.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-지만 - but
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 지만 is a clean hinge between two facts that pull in different directions.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach 지만 directly to the verb or adjective stem: 비싸다 becomes 비싸지만, 어렵다 becomes 어렵지만, 가다 becomes 가지만. After a noun, use 이지만 or 지만 depending on the noun ending: 학생이지만, 친구지만.

examples.en: This restaurant is expensive, but it is delicious.
examples.note: A simple contrast between price and taste.
Two different evaluations in one sentence.

examples.en: I am tired, but I will keep studying.
examples.note: 지만 states the obstacle before the decision.

examples.en: I am a student, but I also work.

a.en: It was expensive, but I bought it.

b.en: It is expensive, so/and... should I buy it?

contrastPairs.explanation: 지만 gives a direct contrast. -는데 often sets background and invites the next thought.

b.en: It is tasty. However, it is expensive.

contrastPairs.explanation: 지만 connects inside one sentence; 하지만 starts a new sentence.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not place 하지만 inside the clause like English word order. Use -지만 on the first predicate or start a new sentence with 하지만.

exceptions: Tense usually appears on the final predicate unless the contrast specifically needs past marking.
하지만 and 그렇지만 can start a new sentence; bare 지만 cannot.
For softer topic-shifting contrast, 그런데 may be more natural than 하지만.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-(으)ㄴ/는데도 - even though, and still
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 는데도 says the expected result did not happen. It often carries surprise, frustration, or emphasis.
grammarNotes.formation: Present verbs take -는데도: 비가 오는데도. Adjectives often take -(으)ㄴ데도: 비싼데도, 어려운데도. Past uses -았/었는데도: 먹었는데도. Nouns use 인데도: 주말인데도.

examples.en: Even though it is raining, there are many people.
examples.note: You might expect fewer people, but the opposite is true.

examples.romanization: yeolsimhi haenneundedo gyeolgwa ga an joasseoyo.
examples.en: Even though I worked hard, the result was not good.
examples.note: The speaker feels the expected result failed to happen.

examples.en: Even though I ate, I am hungry.
examples.note: Past action plus surprising current result.

examples.en: Even though it is the weekend, I have to go to work.

a.en: I worked hard, but I failed.

b.en: Even though I worked hard, I still failed.

contrastPairs.explanation: 지만 is a neutral contrast. -는데도 emphasizes disappointment or surprise.

a.en: I will go even if it rains.

b.en: Even though it is raining, there are many people.

contrastPairs.explanation: -아/어도 often states a condition. -는데도 reacts to an actual situation and unexpected result.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 는데도 already carries the 'even though/still' force. You do not always need to add 그래도.

exceptions: In speech, -는데도 can sound emotional; use -지만 for a calmer contrast.
Adjectives use -(으)ㄴ데도, not always -는데도: 비싼데도, 어려운데도.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어도 - even if / even though
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -아/어도 says the result holds despite the condition.
grammarNotes.formation: Make the 아/어 form and add 도: 가다 becomes 가도, 오다 becomes 와도, 먹다 becomes 먹어도, 하다 becomes 해도. It can be used with adjectives too in common speech: 비싸도, 바빠도, 어려워도.

examples.en: I will go even if it rains.
It does not matter even if it is expensive.
I will keep going even if I am tired.
Even if it is difficult, I will give it a try.

a.en: If it rains, I will not go.

b.en: Even if it rains, I will go.

contrastPairs.explanation: -(으)면 makes the result depend on the condition. -아/어도 says the result stays the same.

a.en: It was expensive, but I bought it.

b.en: I will buy it even if it is expensive.

contrastPairs.explanation: 지만 reports actual contrast. -아/어도 can state a condition or concession.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 오다 contracts to 와 before 도.

exceptions: For adjectives ending in ㅂ, the form changes: 어렵다 becomes 어려워도.
괜찮아요 and 상관없어요 are common second clauses after -아/어도.
Use -지 않아도 for 'even if not': 안 가도 돼요 means you do not have to go.

exampleSentence.en: It is good. But it is a little expensive.
It is delicious. However, it is expensive.
exampleSentence.note: Use at the start of a new sentence.

exampleSentence.en: It is a little inconvenient. However, it is possible.
exampleSentence.note: A slightly fuller form of 하지만.

exampleSentence.en: It is expensive. Even so, shall we try going?
exampleSentence.note: 그래도 keeps the plan or feeling despite the previous sentence.
A core contrast adjective for shopping and restaurants.

exampleSentence.en: It is cheap, but the quality is good.
Even if it is easy, you can make a mistake.
I will continue even if I am tired.
I will keep going even if it is hard.
It is okay even if there is a problem.
There are drawbacks too, but there are more advantages.
Even if there is a drawback, I am okay with it.
It is okay even if it is a little inconvenient.
It is a little inconvenient, but possible.
It does not matter even if it is expensive.

extendedDialogue.setting: Friends decide whether to go to a popular restaurant despite price, crowds, and rain.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: This restaurant is expensive, but really delicious.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: But there are too many people today.
lines.grammarNote: 그런데 softens the turn into a concern.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Even if there are many people, the food comes out quickly.
lines.grammarNote: -아/어도 keeps the result despite the condition.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Even though it is raining, there are many people waiting.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Even so, shall we try going?
lines.grammarNote: 그래도 keeps the plan alive despite the problem.

readingText.title: A good plan with drawbacks
readingText.body: 민서는 새 식당에 가 보고 싶었어요. 그 식당은 비싸지만 음식이 맛있고 서비스도 좋다고 했어요. 지훈은 사람이 너무 많아서 걱정했지만, 민서는 사람이 많아도 음식이 빨리 나온다고 말했어요. 밖에는 비가 오는데도 기다리는 사람이 많았어요. 지훈은 조금 불편해도 괜찮다고 했고, 두 사람은 그래도 한번 가 보기로 했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo wanted to try a new restaurant. It was expensive, but people said the food was good and the service was good. Jihoon worried because there were many people, but Minseo said the food comes out quickly even when it is crowded. Even though it was raining, many people were waiting. They decided to try going anyway.

culturalNote.title: Softening disagreement
culturalNote.body: In Korean conversation, contrast markers can soften disagreement. 그런데 introduces a concern gently, 하지만 is clearer and firmer, and 그래도 keeps a plan or feeling alive after acknowledging the problem.
culturalNote.tip: For a friendly disagreement, start with 맞아요 or 좋아요, then add 그런데: 좋아요. 그런데 조금 비싸요.

inlineExercises.explanation: -아/어도 means even if or even though.

Fix the sentence: 비가 오아도 가요.
inlineExercises.explanation: 오다 contracts to 와 before 도.

bullets: -는데도 adds surprise or frustration: 비가 오는데도 사람이 많아요.
-아/어도 keeps the result despite the condition: 비가 와도 갈 거예요.
그런데, 하지만, and 그래도 differ in tone: soft concern, clear contrast, and even-so continuation.
